A biofilm is defined as a community of microorganisms attached to an inert or living surface.
●     Describe and explain the relationship between quorum sensing and the establishment of a biofilm.
●     Give one (1) example of a biofilm.

Biofilms are a community of microorganisms attached to a surface. Microbial biofilms are complex communities of bacteria and are common in the human body and in the environment. An example is dental plaque. It enhances the bacteria’s resistance to both the host’s defense system and antimicrobials. Quorum sensing is the ability to detect and to respond to cell population density by gene regulation. Quorum sensing allows bacteria to synchronize the gene expression of the group and act in unison using an autoinducer. They undergo behaviors that are carried out as a group and could not be done alone.
Key Points
   Biofilms
are a community of microorganisms
   Common in the human body and in the environment
   Quorum sensing is the ability to detect and to respond to cell population density by gene regulation
   Allows bacteria to synchronize the gene expression of the group
   Some examples of diseases caused by biofilms: dental plaque, otitis media, diabetic wounds, urinary tract infections
